change: Accumulate internal publication holder roots across rejected/incomplete attempts in publish and record_set; release only after successful durable staging. Prevent a conflicting retry from removing the original dependency protection before returning IdempotencyConflict. Public retain still replaces its owner roots.

verification.baseline_public_regressions: All four new API/conflict combinations fail on the preceding wheel at post-conflict GC
verification.prior_101_tlc_algorithm_config_and_state: unchanged; EnvironmentInputs additionally defines conflicting root choices

scope.rust: The actual holding.rs set-union loop is proved for arbitrary input sizes, conditional on ENV-STRING-ORDER (String obeys vstd ordered-key laws). The library law, closure decoding, BTreeSet-to-Vec conversion, catalog append/serialization and call-site staging/release correspondence remain unproved. No new project assume/admit/external-body bypasses.
scope.tla: Three finite positive configurations and three algorithm-negative configurations. Starts after a durable hold and interrupted publication with the original source released; catalog changes are atomic/durable, GC interleaves. Negative controls select TypeOK and NoLostDependency to explore past earlier hold-invariant violations. Progress additionally assumes a correct retry and weak fairness. Full byte replay, actual closures, sealing and all publication failure/recovery paths are not composed.
scope.environment: ENV-PUBLICATION-RETRY permits changed retry roots and GC between protocol steps, supplies complete immutable closures and prohibits peers from mutating another writer internal holder. It does not permit releasing a source after an arbitrary failed API call; the initial hold must already be durable. ENV-STRING-ORDER is separately reviewable and not derived.
scope.measurement: Callback EIO after data fsync, no service crash. Baseline actually deletes the original dependency needed by an uncertain, unacknowledged destination. Fixed cases complete a correct retry, read original/result and reclaim all packs. Four hosts use independent pools rather than shared-pool concurrency.
scope.limits: Abandoned attempts may retain extra roots indefinitely. This fix supplies no cross-process/global idempotency guarantee, automatic abort cleanup, runtime memory bound or new catalog format. Timing groups have n=8 baseline and n=40 fixed; nearest-rank p99 equals sample maximum and cannot become an environment delay bound. No physical 100 GB/TB throughput rerun.

observations_for_spec_review.observed_sequence: durable internal hold -> after_data_sync error -> source release -> conflicting retry rejects -> GC; the old retry removed protection before its rejection
observations_for_spec_review.algorithm_obligation: Preserve previous roots across rejection, permit additive protection, then stage before releasing the operation hold
observations_for_spec_review.numeric_scope: One original source pack and one alternative source per API probe; finite model configurations are exploration bounds, not measured support maxima. Actual union proof covers arbitrary set/input sizes.

measurement.scope: Four hosts independently exercise private pools on JuiceFS, two APIs and two conflicting dependency changes. Callback EIO after data sync, no filesystem/service crash. Sources release after an observed durable internal hold. Baseline loses needed dependencies of an uncertain, unacknowledged publication; fixed retries complete, read and reclaim. Timings include normal metadata/barrier work; caches and background load uncontrolled. Each API/conflict timing group has n=8 baseline and n=40 fixed, so nearest-rank p99 equals its sample maximum. No latency bound or throughput claim.
